title: On Resolving the matter in a single meeting
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：resolve　|　正文 362 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 resolve 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the gardener ① resolved the matter in a single meeting without a word of thanks, and every apprentice in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three springs on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the gardener ② resolves the matter in a single meeting at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ resolve the matter in a single meeting at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ resolved the matter in a single meeting before — a line in the notebook for April 1944 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Resolving the matter in a single meeting without a word of thanks, the gardener said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ resolve to write every week thereafter at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Resolve to write every week thereafter at once and never mention it again.

By 1957 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new apprentice from the next garden ⑧ resolves to write every week thereafter without a word of thanks every spring without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bed, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ resolved the matter in a single meeting again when nobody else would.

⑩ To resolve the matter in a single meeting, my mother said in 1962, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody resolves the matter in a single meeting at once again and somebody must resolve the matter in a single meeting without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 解决（一般过去式 resolved the matter in a single meeting：1950 年园丁头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 解决（一般现在 resolves the matter in a single meeting：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 解决（不定式 to resolve the matter in a single meeting：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 解决（过去完成时 had resolved the matter in a single meeting：1944 年四月的园艺笔记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 解决（动名词 resolving the matter in a single meeting 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 决心（resolve to write every week thereafter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去决心此后决心每周写一封信）
G. v. 决心（resolve to write every week thereafter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 解决（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 resolves to write every week thereafter，而母亲又一次 resolved the matter in a single meeting）

answers.why: resolve 意为“解决”，1950 年园丁不图一句谢解决一次会就把那件事解决了，那是园子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 resolved。
resolve 意为“解决”，自那以后园丁二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 resolves。
resolve 意为“解决”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯解决一次会就把那件事解决了”，此处为不定式 to resolve the matter in a single meeting。
resolve 意为“解决”，园艺笔记里 四月 那行字说明早在 1957 年之前就有人解决过，故用过去完成时 had resolved。
resolve 意为“解决”，园丁说“解决一次会就把那件事解决了这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 resolving the matter in a single meeting 作主语。
resolve 意为“决心”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去决心此后决心每周写一封信”，should ever 之后用原形 resolve to write every week thereafter。
resolve 意为“决心”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻决心此后决心每周写一封信（resolve to write every week thereafter at once），以后再也不要提起。
resolve 意为“解决”，新来的学徒每个春天都照例决心此后决心每周写一封信，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 resolves。
resolve 意为“解决”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢解决一次会就把那件事解决了，用一般过去式 resolved 叙述。
resolve 意为“解决”，结尾那句是母亲 1962 年的话：要解决一次会就把那件事解决了，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和园子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 resolve 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the gardener resolved the matter in a single meeting without a word of thanks, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the gardener resolves the matter in a single meeting at once whenever the garden asks.
Resolving the matter in a single meeting without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever resolve to write every week thereafter at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next garden resolves to write every week thereafter without a word of thanks every spring, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother resolved the matter in a single meeting again, and the garden remembered that half.
